$schema-note: Hand-written and pasted HTML: the input class the CommonMark and GFM corpora cannot contain, because they are HTML written by cmark in exactly the vocabulary this tool's pipeline emits. Read by scripts/generate-pasted-html-oracle.mjs, which runs every document through the tool, renders each pair of documents in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and commits what the engines saw to pasted-html.oracle.json. Read by pasted-html.test.ts, which holds every census note to that answer.

provenance.hand-written:
Written for this corpus, in the shapes people type: no

where one is optional,

provenance.export-shape: The markup a product is known to emit, RECONSTRUCTED here rather than captured - the ids, classes, inline styles and wrapper elements that characterise the format - around text written for this corpus. None of these products can be driven from this repository, so the shape rests on knowledge of the format, and the entry says which features it is reproducing. Weaker than a capture and stated as such.
provenance.clipboard: Captured: a real Ctrl+C in a real engine over a page scripts/capture-pasted-html.mjs serves itself, read back through navigator.clipboard.read(). What a browser's own serialiser puts on the clipboard, which is the machine-made half of pasted HTML. Chromium and Firefox only: WebKit's async clipboard returns no items to a read in Playwright's build, measured, so there is no WebKit capture rather than an imitation of one.
